stemMarkdown: A train 120 m long is running at 72 km/h. How many seconds does it take to pass a telegraph pole? (Round to 4 decimal places.)
solutionMarkdown: To pass a pole the train must cover its own length. Speed $= 72 \times \dfrac{5}{18} = 20.0000$ m/s, so time $= \dfrac{120}{20.0000} = 6.0$ seconds.
altSolutionMarkdown: A pole has no length, so the distance is exactly the train's length — nothing else.
